questions.question: Where can nonzero entries appear in an upper triangular matrix?
options: On or above the main diagonal.
Only in the first column.
Only on the anti-diagonal.
Only below the main diagonal.

questions.question: What must be zero in an upper triangular matrix?
options: All entries above the main diagonal.
All entries in the first row.
All diagonal entries.
All entries below the main diagonal.

questions.question: What is the determinant of an upper triangular matrix?
options: The product of its diagonal entries.
The product of all entries above the diagonal.
The sum of its diagonal entries.
Always zero.

questions.question: Why is every diagonal matrix upper triangular?
options: It has zeros below the main diagonal.
It has no entries above the main diagonal.
It must be a row vector.
It has determinant one.

questions.question: How do upper and lower triangular matrices differ in their zero pattern?
options: Upper triangular matrices have zeros below the diagonal; lower triangular matrices have zeros above it.
Upper triangular matrices have no diagonal entries.
Upper triangular matrices must be nonsingular; lower triangular matrices must be singular.
Lower triangular matrices are not square.

questions.question: Which matrix is upper triangular?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\2&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: When is an upper triangular matrix guaranteed to be singular?
options: When at least one diagonal entry is zero.
When all entries below the diagonal are zero.
When its trace is positive.
When at least one entry above the diagonal is nonzero.

questions.question: Why can entries above the diagonal be ignored when computing the determinant of an upper triangular matrix?
options: The triangular zero pattern makes the determinant equal to the diagonal product.
Those entries are not part of the matrix, irrespective of the particular case.
They are always equal to one.
They determine the trace instead.

options: It is never triangular unless both factors are identity matrices.
It is again upper triangular.
It is always diagonal.
It is always lower triangular.
